anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine runtime settings are mis-tuned relative to hardware capacity, workload intensity, or version defaults, causing artificial pressure or idle gaps in internal subsystems.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical or virtual storage layer is saturated for bandwidth, IOPS, or latency, becoming the dominant bottleneck for data, temp, or log files.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Host processors are driven to sustained saturation, producing scheduler back-pressure and broad latency inflation across the workload.

When all three root causes manifest together, the database shows a tangled symptom set: chronic log-write, buffer-I/O, and scheduler waits coexist with high CPU utilisation, long run-queues, and soaring device queue depths. Checkpoint or flush storms triggered by mis-sized memory or aggressive durability settings rapidly fill the storage queues; as write latency increases, foreground sessions stall, yet CPU remains pegged by spin-waits, retry loops, and inflated parallelism. Performance counters may misleadingly suggest that either CPU or I/O alone explains the slowdown, while misconfigured parameters (e.g., tiny shared buffers, oversized work memory, excessive max_parallelism, or aggressive checkpoint_timeout) obscure the true dual-resource crisis. Batch windows elongate, OLTP transactions time out, analytics spill to disk, and background maintenance never catches up, creating an all-round degradation that is hard to attribute to a single tier.

Causally, poor configuration choices can provoke both CPU and I/O stress: undersized cache or too-frequent checkpoints amplify physical reads/writes, driving the storage layer into throughput saturation; in turn, the heightened I/O latency causes the engine to hold latches and spin longer, inflating CPU consumption. Simultaneously, mis-set parallelism or memory parameters increase CPU demand and plan concurrency, further intensifying I/O issuance rates. The saturated storage responds with even longer latencies, which stall worker threads and trigger additional background activity (e.g., checkpoints, log flushes), creating a feedback loop that deepens both CPU and I/O contention. The intertwined effects of misconfiguration, device saturation, and compute exhaustion therefore reinforce one another, dragging overall database performance into a severe, multi-resource bottleneck state.

entry.official_definition: The time limit for regular expression matching operations performed by the regular expression engine.
entry.trigger_condition: A regular expression match operation exceeds regexp_time_limit.
entry.workload_impact: The regular expression operation is constrained by the configured time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
